passage: Since opening in 2016, the Copenhagen Water Treatment Facility—an innovative waste management plant in Denmark that features a recreational ski slope built on its roof—has gained international attention as a symbol of sustainable urban design. Architect Bjarke Ingels designed the facility, which processes the city's wastewater while providing year-round skiing opportunities, to demonstrate that industrial infrastructure can enhance rather than detract from urban life. However, the concept has drawn criticism: skeptics argue that while the facility's engineering systems were extensively tested before construction, it remains uncertain whether the dual-purpose design can maintain operational efficiency over time.
prompt: According to the text, why are some critics skeptical of the concept behind the Copenhagen Water Treatment Facility?

choices.A: Key features of the facility's design would be challenging to implement in cities other than Copenhagen.
choices.B: It is uncertain whether the facility can continue to function effectively with its current design.
choices.C: The recreational activities available at the facility turned out to be more limited than Ingels had originally planned.
choices.D: The facility's construction required significantly more resources than building separate waste treatment and recreational facilities would have required.

explanation: Choice B is the best answer because it accurately describes the critics' concerns as stated in the text. The text explains that Ingels designed the facility to demonstrate that industrial infrastructure can enhance urban life, but critics argue that it remains uncertain whether the dual-purpose design can maintain operational efficiency over time. Therefore, according to the text, critics are skeptical because it is uncertain whether the facility can continue to function effectively with its current design.
